html:
Guests check out, and the bedrooms are usually fine. The living room is another story. When our team walks into a Greer vacation rental after a family weekend, the couch cushions are shifted, a throw blanket is on the floor, and there is a half-finished puzzle or a phone charger still plugged in behind the TV stand. That is why Airbnb cleaning for the living room and shared spaces deserves its own routine, separate from the bathrooms and bedrooms.

Below is how we reset the main living area of a short-term rental in Greer, in the order we do it, plus what hosts can do to make each turnover easier. It applies whether your place is a house near Downtown Greer, a rental close to GSP Airport or a home off SC-14 that fills up on BMW and travel-nurse weeks.

What the living room looks like after a stay

Shared spaces take the most traffic and the least attention from guests. Some things we find again and again:

  • Crumbs, popcorn and pet hair pushed deep into sofa seams
  • Rings and sticky spots on coffee tables and end tables
  • Remote controls and game controllers with a film of hand oil
  • Fingerprints on the TV screen, glass tabletops and sliding door
  • Pillows and throws moved to bedrooms and never returned
  • Items left behind, from earbuds to children's toys

None of this is the guests' fault. It is simply what a lived-in room looks like after three or four days, and it all needs to be gone before the next check-in.

Our order of work in a shared space

1. Walk the room before touching anything

We look first. Damage, stains, a missing lamp shade or a wobbly chair gets a photo before we start, because a damage and missing-item report with photos is part of the service. Doing it first means the photo shows what the guest left, not what we disturbed.

2. Collect and remove

Cups, wrappers, stray dishes and trash go out first. Cushions come off the sofa so we can see what is underneath.

3. Dust high to low

Shelves, picture frames, TV stand, lamps and ceiling fan blades come before the floor, so nothing we knock loose lands on a clean surface. Microfiber is damp enough to pick up dust instead of moving it around.

4. Wipe the touch points

Remotes, light switches, door handles, the thermostat and the arms of chairs get wiped and sanitized. These are the spots a new guest handles in the first five minutes.

5. Floors last

Vacuum under the cushions and along the edge of the sofa, then vacuum and mop the room, finishing at the door so we do not walk back over a wet floor.

6. Stage to match the listing

Pillows go back where the photos show them, the throw is folded, the coffee table is styled the way you listed it, and the host-provided guidebook sits where guests will find it. A room that looks like your photos earns better reviews than one that is merely clean.

Shared spaces that hosts forget

The living room is rarely alone. Most Greer rentals also have an entry, a hallway, a dining nook or a screened porch that guests use constantly. We include them in the same pass:

SpaceWhat we check
EntrywayShoe tray, mat, hooks, door glass
Dining nookTable, chair seats, crumbs on the floor underneath
HallwayBaseboards, light switches, scuffs near corners
Porch or patio doorGlass, track, outdoor furniture surfaces

Hosts who also read about the other rooms can find the bathroom routine in Airbnb cleaning in Greer: bathrooms done right, which pairs well with this one.

Same-day turnovers and the living room

Tight windows change the order. When a guest checks out at 11 and the next arrives mid-afternoon, the living room is often the first space we finish, because it is the first room a new guest walks into. We reset it while other rooms are still in progress, then do a last look at the end to catch anything that moved. Hosts who run several turnovers a month tell us the biggest relief is not having to check this room themselves. If you are weighing a weekly schedule against ad hoc visits, our Greer Airbnb cleaning service lets you describe the pattern, and we plan around it. Hosts who live out of town especially value the photo report, since it shows the room as left and as reset.

A few host habits that make the living room easier

  • Keep decor simple. Every extra pillow and trinket is one more thing to put back.
  • Use washable throws and slipcovers where you can.
  • Take a photo of the room as it should look and keep it in the guidebook or send it to us.
  • Leave a lidded trash can and a small basket for remotes so they do not wander.

faqs: Do you clean under the sofa cushions during a turnover?
Yes. Cushions come off so we can vacuum the seams and the frame, since that is where crumbs and pet hair collect during a stay.
Can you restage the living room to match my listing photos?
Yes. Staging to match your listing photos is part of the Airbnb service. Sending us a reference photo of the room helps us place pillows and decor the same way each time.
What happens if a guest breaks or removes something from the living room?
We note it in the damage and missing-item report and attach photos, so you can follow up with the guest or platform quickly.
